items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-19
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Fats Waller; INTERVIEWEE does not mention Fats Waller in their response, only discussing Rudy Valli, Dick Stabile, and Charlie Parker.

ctx.x: No, he says that he did everything he could to make it possible for himself to sound like...

But jazz musicians are always notorious. Like Fats Waller plays... I said he played organ, and he liked some organ player. He did like... Who was the most smeltsy organ player in the world. And there was no way by listening to Fats Waller's music that you were going to say... Yes. ...that he was influenced by that organ.

Well, what I am saying is that if you listen to Rudy Valli, and especially to Dick Stabile on records... Yeah. And if you listen to them... You're going to hear all those fast changes that Parker makes? You're going to hear all those things that Parker makes. I don't believe it. Well, try it and see. I don't believe that. I recommend that you try it and see. Yeah. Because it'll be illuminating for you to do that. And I considered that Charlie Parker was very pleasant. He had a tendency to be narcissistic. He was…
